Welcome aboard! Your project currently shows a standalone subscription page replica (the October Issue offer with Digital / Print + Digital plans) that works as a plain HTML file. Here are natural next steps, roughly in order of impact:

  1. Make it real — Connect a payment provider (Stripe or Paddle) so the "Get Digital Access" button actually starts a checkout, instead of the current preview-only dialog.
  2. Add branding — Replace the placeholder blocks (the gray brand/logo boxes in the masthead, hero, and All Access card) with your actual logo and imagery.
  3. Tailor the offer — Adjust the plan names, prices, and terms copy to match your product.
  4. Collect signups — Store the emails entered at checkout in a database, so you can follow up with subscribers even before payments go live.

If you tell me which direction interests you — payments, branding, pricing, or email capture — I'll build it. If you're not sure yet, email capture plus branding is a good low-risk start.

Please make the following changes to this page. Apply them directly to what's already built here, rather than rebuilding it from scratch:

From B1: I would maybe add/change the ones provided because it doesn't seem to have a lot of variation (at least visibly). I think doing something similar to Spotify's sectioning or even just making the differences much more noticeable would be better. I think sectioning it to be 4 groups would be the most ideal: (1) Student; there are a lot of fashion majors at universities that would probably love a discount, or even students who want to see the fashion world, but don't have the money to spend on it would also appreciate the discounted rate (2) Reader; digital only, for people who love to read the details of fashion shows or general information provided in Vogue (3) Collector; someone who appreciates the print of the magazine, not only the content, but likes to collect the physical editions (4) Gift; someone who wants to try it out one time and see if it is worth their money and gets a gift to incentivize the continued purchase/subscription. From B2: I would probably use the $.99 because it feels like a better deal for the customer, but in actuality is the best price for the company as well. Often the $.00 signals luxury, which we could apply to a certain subscription if we want it to give that idea to the customers, but Vogue is more about trendy fashion that should be affordable for people to view. This is an example of psychological pricing. From B3: I would use per month because it would seem to be cheaper than stating the accumulated amount per year. More frequent numbers feel less costly than the larger lump sum. From B4: Yes. It comes across as a reference point and makes the consumer feel as though they should jump on the "sale/discount" at that time in order to save money. It is perceived as a deal and creates pleasure for the subscriber to actually follow through and use the product. From B5: No From B6: Yes because u ...

Updated subscription page

I've applied the changes to the subscription page:

  • Four groups: the plans now sit under four tabs: Student, Reader, Collector and Gift. Each has a one-line description.
  • Pricing: every price ends in .99 and is shown per month, with a crossed-out original price and a "Save %" tag.
  • Preselected plan: each group opens with one plan already picked. Reader opens on Annual Digital, the Best Offer.
  • Comparison: every plan has a checklist that marks which benefits it includes and which it doesn't.
  • Fine print: the renewal terms are now smaller and lighter. I didn't hide any fees.
  • New options: I added student discounts, Print + Digital, and an All Access Premium tier that's the only plan with every benefit.
  • Gift: these are 3-month trials, and the Print + Digital one includes a free tote.
  • Price level: prices are slightly higher than before, closer to Cosmopolitan's. Annual Digital went from $1 to $1.99 a month, and the offer at the top of the page now matches.

I made up the exact prices and some benefit names, like "Runway archive" and "Members-only events". Send me your real figures and I'll swap them in.

I made no changes for the "From B5: No" note, because without the original question I couldn't tell what it referred to.
